Sara — thanks, appreciate the clear asks. Pushing a short summary + proposed tradeoffs below so legal can see the options.

Proposal (high level):
- Option A (Operational priority): 99.95% monthly uptime for Dedicated pools; 99.9% for Standard. Maintenance windows: up to 8 hours per week planned maintenance across "maintenance windows" (we propose a single 2am-6am local window, weekly cadence) with 72-hour advance notice for planned events. Service credits: scaled per percentage point below SLA (attached SLA_matrix.xlsx).
- Option B (Customer credit priority): 99.95% for both tiers, but maintenance windows limited to 4 hours/week and credits increased by ~1.5x in the <99.9 band. This will have cost implications — I will ask Marcus to quantify.

Key constraints:
- Emergency maintenance (security hotfixes) can be performed with 2-hour notice; we want to preserve that carveout for P0 security issues.
- Rolling kernel upgrades require a 48-hour maintenance slot per region; if NovaMed requires no rolling windows we will need to scope Dedicated isolation and scheduling costs.

Attachments: redline_summary.docx (brief covering note), SLA_matrix.xlsx (proposed credit table).

Next steps:
- Kimberly: can Legal review the two options and flag must-haves vs negotiables?
- Marcus: can you run a rough delta on cost for Option B vs A and paste numbers here?
- Sara: if either option looks workable, we can circulate a redline Order Form (v3) for countersign.

I will hold a short sync at 3pm PST if helpful — happy to include Emma from Wilson Legal.

Best,

Aditya / team — reading through Option A and B. High-level legal guidance and our recommended carveouts below (short). Quoting your note: "Emergency maintenance (security hotfixes) 2-hour notice" — we can accept that with a narrow definition and audit trail requirements.

Legal recommendations (must-haves in any counter):
- Define "Availability" clearly (host-level v. region-level calculation). We should propose a single-source measurement (our telemetry) but allow NovaMed a weekly CSV export for auditing.
- Planned maintenance: require advance notice (>=72 hours) and show a maximum weekly window (we can compromise on hours but need a cap).
- Emergency maintenance: narrow to "critical security vulnerabilities requiring immediate mitigation" and require post-event report within 48 hours.
- Credits: cap aggregate monthly credits at 50% of monthly invoice for severe multi-region outages — we should avoid uncapped exposure.
- Data retention / logs: NovaMed asked for a 12-month audit log retention; we can do 12 months standard with an add-on for longer retention.

Operational asks for Finance/Ops (Marcus): please annotate the SLA_matrix and provide an estimated 12-month run-rate delta for Option B. If Option B increases expected cost, include a single-year and three-year projection.

I'll take a pass on redline language this afternoon and circulate a tracked-change PDF.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Copying into the thread my decision items so we get to a clean offer for NovaMed tomorrow:

1) Differentiate by service tier: Dedicated = 99.95% / Standard = 99.9%. This keeps sales motion simple and gives procurement a clear upgrade path.
2) Planned maintenance: cap at 6 hours/week (we settle at 6 rather than 8) with 72-hour notice.
3) Emergency maintenance carveout OK but must have strict definition and a mandatory 48-hour follow-up report to NovaMed.
4) Cap aggregate monthly credits at 50% invoice. No uncapped liability.

Marcus — please prioritize the Option B delta, but note that if NovaMed insists on 99.95 for both tiers we likely need to introduce a monthly minimum contract value or price uplift for Standard.

Aditya — get the redline to Sara with these bullets + attachments by EOD tomorrow. If procurement pushes back on the maintenance cap, authorize up to a single compromise call with finance and legal present.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success (interim)
